items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia chief executive following reports of three affairs, leaving the company without a permanent successor and no succession plan. Prediction market Kalshi showed odds for naming Huang next permanent CEO rose to 15% before falling to around 7%, while Ian Buck leads at 33%. Colette Kress sits at 13%. Tech figures including Elon Musk and Donald Trump voiced support, with Trump suggesting Tim Cook as successor; Polymarket implied a 6% chance for Cook. Nvidia shares rebounded from US$150 to around US$162 after the ousting.
items.title: Prediction Markets Bet on Jensen Huang's Return as Nvidia CEO Amid Succession Uncertainty

items.summary: NVIDIA's cuBLAS, in CUDA Toolkit 13.4.2, accelerates full double-precision (FP64) dense matrix multiplications by breaking numbers into integer pieces and multiplying them exactly on GPU Tensor Cores via the Automatic Dynamic Precision framework. Two new algorithms—Ozaki-II, which needs roughly half the GEMMs of Ozaki-I at FP64 accuracy, and a 2M complex-multiply method—are chosen automatically with no code changes. DGEMM runs up to 5.5x faster on VR NVL72 and 3.9x on GB200; CCSD quantum-chemistry workloads reach 11.5x over native FP64, while BerkeleyGW materials simulations gain 6.6x.
items.title: NVIDIA cuBLAS FP64 Emulation Speeds Double-Precision Matrix Math on Tensor Cores

items.summary: An extramarital affair has renewed global scrutiny on chip giant Nvidia and its Singapore-based client Megaspeed, which is suspected of helping China access advanced US semiconductors barred from export. Observers told CNA that the saga could soon make things trickier for Singapore in the semiconductor space. Matthias Hendrichs noted Singapore's deep ties with both Washington and Beijing mean it has less room to manoeuvre on this technology. Associate Professor Chong Ja Ian warned of a 'Singapore washing' perception, though Singapore does not implement unilateral foreign export controls. Analysts expect more US pressure, tighter rules for Southeast Asia, higher compliance costs and slower transactions, affecting the trading side rather than manufacturing.
items.title: Nvidia-Megaspeed Saga Could Squeeze Singapore's Room in Chips Space, Slow Things for Firms: Analysts

items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 31.53 points (0.42%) to 7,560.87 while the Nasdaq dropped 230.13 points (0.91%), but the Dow rose 46.14 points (0.09%). Nvidia's sixth straight weekly decline followed CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid personal-conduct revelations; Arm Holdings' Rene Haas is a potential successor, raising AI-trade concerns. Weak October producer prices still supported at least a 25-basis-point December Fed hike.
items.title: US Stocks Close Lower on Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty and Rate-Hike Bets

items.summary: A global outage of Microsoft's Outlook and Teams eased after more than 24 hours, though the company gave no timeline for full recovery. Server issues caused the incident, which also affected its Copilot AI assistant; Microsoft ruled out malicious activity and AI as causes. A broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing systems. The two workplace applications serve hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook and Teams Outage Eases After More Than a Day

items.summary: On Friday (local time), Microsoft apologized to customers and partners after a global outage disrupted services including Outlook email, Microsoft Teams and Copilot. The company attributed the incident to a technical issue linked to an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change, explicitly ruling out any cyberattack or AI-agent involvement. The disruption affected at least 74 countries, including the United States, leaving millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours and impacting airline operations worldwide, prompting major Indian carriers to issue passenger advisories.
items.title: Microsoft Apologizes After Global Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot for Nearly 18 Hours

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped down after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, who ran Megaspeed, a major Nvidia chip buyer. The case has spotlighted tensions in Singapore's role as a global semiconductor hub. Last year it was Nvidia's second-largest market globally, yet less than 1% of its earnings came from chips physically present there, since the island routes orders onward to Asia. Since US export restrictions on advanced chips reached China in 2022, officials worry countries like Singapore could be used for illicit access; Megaspeed is suspected of giving Chinese firms backdoor chip access via data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. Singapore has charged four companies and five individuals but brought no charges against Megaspeed-linked parties after finding insufficient evidence against Alice Huang.
items.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore

items.summary: On Friday, a regulatory filing revealed that Soros Fund Management significantly increased its third-quarter stake in Intel, building a 2.83 million-share position valued at $340.3 million from just 100,000 shares held by end of June.
items.title: Soros Fund Management Ramps Up Intel Stake in Q3

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage struck the UK on Friday, causing serious and widespread disruption across healthcare, courts, police and property services. The NHS reported hundreds of hospitals, GP surgeries and community health services affected as staff lost access to email, meetings and patient data; some fell back on paper records while operations were cancelled or delayed. Courts saw cases at magistrates', crown and civil levels — including in Manchester and Scotland — postponed after the judiciary's reliance on Microsoft platforms. Police online reporting was down but 999 remained unaffected, with staff returning to phone contact. Property agents relied on direct communication as end-of-week moves continued.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Key UK Public Services

items.summary: Despite co-founding and leading Nvidia for 33 years, Jensen Huang's roughly 870 million shares—about 3.6% of the company—did not grant him absolute control. Nearly 800 million were held via trusts shared with his wife; about 70 million directly. His November 12 resignation underscores that large ownership does not guarantee board authority.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Shareholding Fell Short of Board Control

items.summary: Four federal agencies—the Federal Reserve Board, FDIC, NCUA, and OCC—announced on November 13, 2026, that they will extend the comment period for proposed third-party risk management guidance until December 16. Originally due November 16, comments now target supervisory experience-based principles designed to help banks and credit unions tailor practices to individual relationships. The non-binding guidance is intended to be rescinded upon finalization.
items.title: Federal Agencies Extend Comment Period for Third-Party Risk Management Guidance

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid reports of relationships with two employees, including Alice Huang, suspected by US intelligence of working for Beijing; a third woman was also linked to him. Separately, Microsoft suffered one of its worst outages after taking over as the world's most valuable company, lasting at least 18 hours due to server overload and unexpected unavailability.
items.title: Microsoft Outage and Nvidia Leadership Fallout

items.summary: Jensen Huang's sudden resignation has raised questions about who will lead the world's most prominent AI chip company, with interim CFO Collete Kriss named. Among seven candidates discussed are Ian Buck, Lisa Su of AMD, Rene Haas of Arm, John Srouji of Apple, and former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger.
items.title: Seven Candidates Emerge for Nvidia CEO Role After Jensen Huang's Resignation

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang (Huang Le), a suspected Chinese spy. Sen. Tim Scott requested that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee, warning he could be subpoenaed if he declines. Huang was also summoned by House committees for a December 1 interview.
items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Summoned by Congress Over Spy Scandal

items.summary: A failure in Microsoft's server infrastructure has cut users off from Outlook email, Teams and Copilot for more than a day, with problems reported across 74 countries. The disruption began Thursday afternoon European time and was still not fully fixed Friday morning; by then Microsoft reported only marginal success after overnight fixes crashed again under returning traffic. No cyber attack is indicated, though speculation persists amid no confirmed cause or timeline. Beyond missed emails, the outage affected UK GP practices, Singapore's government, Australian intelligence services, OpenAI and Anthropic, and Workhorse postponed an earnings call. Experts warn of Europe's heavy reliance on a handful of US tech giants.
items.title: Microsoft outage explained: what went wrong and is your data at risk?

items.summary: Google and Samsung announced preorders for a line of smart glasses, released in partnership with eyewear brands Gentle Monster (six styles) and Warby Parker (three models), challenging category leader Meta. The nine styles ship around Dec. 10 at $449 or $395, weigh about 41 grams, offer up to nine hours of battery life, and include a charging case with seven top-ups. They run on Android XR, feature HDR cameras, binaural audio, navigation, translation, and Gemini AI integration, compatible with iPhones and select Google/Samsung devices. Emphasizing privacy amid Meta’s pushback—nicknamed “pervert glasses”—Google will disable recording if the indicator light is tampered with, redact bystander faces before processing, require user consent agreements, and restrict apps from live-streaming or facial identification.
items.title: Google and Samsung Set to Release AI Smart Glasses in December

items.summary: IndiGo, India's largest airline, said Friday its email support was disrupted by a global Microsoft service outage beginning late Thursday night. The carrier rerouted emails to maintain uninterrupted communication and continued responding within its usual 24-hour timeline, while confirming all other channels remain available and flight operations unaffected. Microsoft attributed the strain—not increased traffic—to servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable, with no evidence of malicious activity as of an 11:16 am IST service-health update.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Impacts IndiGo's Email Support Services

items.summary: The Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission’s Menhaden Management Board cut coastwide catch limits by about 9 percent in both 2027 and 2028, reducing the total allowable catch from 170,000 metric tons to 155,000 metric tons. The Chesapeake Bay cap fell further—by 27 percent then 34 percent—and tied reduction fishing to 21.8 percent of the coastwide limit. Conservationists welcomed the cuts but warned they fall short: a deeper cut would only yield a 50 percent chance of meeting an ecological target that excludes ospreys, whose Bay nesting success dropped sharply. The industry pushed back, citing economic harm and calling for research before further restrictions.
items.title: ASMFC Lowers Menhaden Caps Despite Conservationist Concerns

items.summary: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, delaying or canceling more than 11,000 flights across the US and plunging airports into chaos. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed it to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” while DHS Director Markwayne Mullin said preliminary investigations showed no indication of a nefarious attack, calling it instead a telecommunications outage. Officials prioritized landing airborne aircraft but offered no timeline for resuming departures. CNN reported the FAA blamed router malfunctions originating at Chicago Midway airport that rippled nationwide. This was the third such grounding in US history, following 9/11 and January 2023.
items.title: FAA Nationwide Ground Stop Disrupts US Airports

items.summary: Jojo, an 11-year-old male gorilla rescued as an infant from Gabon's private zoo where his family was killed by poachers, has spent nearly his entire life alone. His carers at the Lekedi Foundation want to find him a companion, possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla. Researchers including Prof Gillian Forrester of Sussex and Dr Robin Morrison of Zurich note that being bonded with others is vital for great ape psychology; Morrison's study found female mountain gorillas seek familiar companions when joining groups. However, no suitable match has emerged despite contacts with accredited zoos, as international translocation rules are built for breeding programmes rather than companion introductions or wild reintroductions.
items.title: Jojo the gorilla seeks a companion after decades of solitary confinement

items.summary: On Nov 13, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower as concerns over Nvidia pressured technology shares. Nvidia's stock fell 2% for its sixth straight week after CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs. The Dow rose modestly to 52,347.55 while the S&P 500 lost 30.73 points and the Nasdaq dropped 229.82 points. For the week, however, all three indexes posted gains as Nvidia's decline snapped a four-week losing streak for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Separately, October producer prices rose 6.5% year over year, keeping expectations for a December rate hike intact.
items.title: US Tech Shares and Inflation Data Weigh on Markets Amid Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: On Friday, US stock indexes fell amid renewed concerns about Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation reignited a technology selloff. The Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 6%, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom falling 10% and 7%. Soft October producer prices data offered little relief as inflation remained elevated at 6.5% year over year, prompting warnings that the AI trade faces fresh headwinds.
items.title: US Stocks Tumble as Nvidia Slides 4.3%, Triggering Fresh Selloff in Technology Shares

items.summary: Per the Financial Times, Nvidia's board approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a successor to Jensen Huang. Reports indicate some employees are pushing to bring back the former chief executive, who stepped down Thursday amid revelations of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy. Analysts had already floated Haas' name; he spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013.
items.title: Nvidia Approaches Arm CEO Haas as Employees Seek Huang's Return

items.summary: Institutional investor interest in Anthropic's initial public offering is outpacing SpaceX's earlier roadshow, with demand growing from roughly two times oversubscribed on day one to six times by Thursday. Bankers attribute the strength to the deal's size and expect continued growth as investors weigh whether Anthropic can sustain its AI lead amid rapid competition from Alphabet's Google. Valuation hinges on projected 2028 revenue of $270 billion to $280 billion, though sell-side estimates for 2026 range from $52 billion to $53 billion and buy-side projections vary further, with some running up to 10% to 15% higher while others sit about 30% below. Limited disclosure during the roadshow has left key questions unanswered.
items.title: Investor Demand and Valuation Uncertainty Surround Anthropic's $64 Billion IPO

items.summary: This item is a single-panel political cartoon by Martin Rowson satirizing Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang, framed around his 'downfall.' The piece offers no accompanying article text, figures, or further context beyond its captioned title. It functions purely as visual commentary rather than reporting on specific events or claims about the company's performance.
items.title: Martin Rowson on the downfall of Nvidia's Jensen Huang – cartoon

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang stepped down after 33 years, sending shockwaves through the startup ecosystem. Investors say his departure removes a dominant champion that backed nearly every AI-native company from application to neocloud, injecting tens of billions annually across 105 rounds this year alone as its largest investor in many deals. His conservative successor Colette Kress is expected to write smaller checks and be more selective, threatening valuations and early-stage funding—especially outside the U.S., where Nvidia's support created a gap no one can fill.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Departure Blasts Big Hole in AI Startup Funding

items.summary: The FTC plans to file suit today to block a $3.5 billion merger of CD&R and TPG-owned Covetrus from acquiring MWI Veterinary Supply, citing increased costs for pet owners and clinics. Officials say the deal would create a highly concentrated market; neither company commented. The move reflects leadership under Andrew Ferguson's focus on affordability in President Trump's agenda.
items.title: FTC Plans to Block $3.5 Billion Veterinary Merger

items.summary: Anthropic's IPO is reportedly six times oversubscribed, signaling investor optimism in the AI sector despite recent tech weakness and a Nasdaq monthly loss its largest in over a year. Nvidia's CEO resignation intensified concerns about spending and debt. Yet some investors remain confident: Goldman Sachs, an underwriter, projects Anthropic's revenue surpassing $600 billion by 2030—more than 130 times last year's sales.
items.title: Demand Remains Strong for Anthropic IPO Despite Tech Pullback

items.summary: Eighteen patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV therapy, have raised concerns they could prolong market exclusivity and delay affordable generics. Patient groups and civil society contest the move with regulatory authorities, arguing the applications lack novelty and inventive steps. The filings exemplify 'evergreening,' where secondary patents on minor variations extend exclusivity to keep prices high and restrict patient access.
items.title: Breakthrough HIV Drug Sees 18 Patent Filings in India, May Delay Affordable Generics

items.summary: The Leh Apex Body's indefinite dharna entered its second day amid intensifying protests against the government's decision to hold Ladakh hill council elections on Dec 4, despite opposition from the LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance. Religious heads would lead a hunger strike from Saturday at NDS memorial park in Leh. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said he was forcibly confined; police denied him leaving his residence after preventive restrictions were imposed for 60 days by the Leh DM.
items.title: Leh Protest Intensifies as Wangchuk Under House Detention

items.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop, halting departures and delays to landings at all airports in the United States. The halt began around 4pm ET on Friday and was caused by what officials described as 'a temporary telecommunications outage.' In its statement, the FAA noted that every flight had been accounted for and that international flights would be handled on a case-by-case basis.
items.title: Rare Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Caused by Telecommunications Outage

items.summary: A quality-control failure forced California regulators to discard nearly nine months of air-monitoring data for the fumigants 1,3-D and methyl bromide. Advocates argue this undermines confidence in new rules limiting worker exposure, which they say are weaker than scientific safety targets—allowing residents up to 14 times higher levels while workers face five times higher ones. Reform groups worry emissions rose after a 2024 residential rule took effect, but DPR plans to replace lost data with unverified models that may underestimate risk.
items.title: California's New Pesticide Regulation May Not Protect Workers Amid Lost Air-Monitoring Data

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid mounting speculation about an alleged espionage plot involving his wife, Alice Huang — a former Megaspeed executive suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy — and two other extra-marital affairs. Congressional Republicans and three House committee chairs are demanding testimony or closed-door interviews from Huang, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Under-Secretary Jeffrey Kessler over AI chip exports to China and stalled trade blacklists. Trump defended Huang despite reports he was briefed on the espionage findings a year ago without acting. Nvidia launched an independent investigation while Colette Kress became interim CEO; it found no evidence of compromised national security or company secrets. Alice Huang, banned from Singapore, reportedly lives in Beijing.
items.title: Questions Left to Answer in Wake of Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary: At the inaugural African-hosted 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, Australia won six medals—four silvers and two bronzes. Nearly 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 competed across 25 sports over two weeks. Boxer Marley Dodd took silver at 55kg; Mackenzie Macdonald earned Australia's first-ever taekwondo medal in the 49kg category; cyclists Elsie Apps and Caleb McKenzie won silver and bronze respectively, with McKenzie recovering from Hashimoto's disease to claim a late sprint victory. Queensland beach volleyball pair Thomas Turner and Ryan Edgar took bronze. IOC President Kirsty Coventry praised the event as exceeding expectations but cautioned that only about 15% of Youth Olympic athletes progress to the full Olympics. China led medal counts with 18 golds, ahead of Japan (11) and Russia (8). The Games marked a milestone for emerging Australian talent heading toward Brisbane 2032.
items.title: Australia's Youth Olympic Medal Haul as Dakar Games Celebrated

items.summary: The South African Supreme Court of Appeal dismissed the government's appeal in the #CancelCoal case, upholding a High Court ruling that struck down plans for 1,500 megawatts of new coal-fired power. Environmental NGOs argued it violated children's constitutional right to a healthy environment, citing over 2,200 annual deaths from air pollution. The Minister can still appeal to the Constitutional Court.
items.title: South African Court Dismisses Appeal Over Planned Coal-Fired Power Plants

items.summary: India's apex drug regulator, the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi, ordered an immediate halt to manufacturing, sale, and distribution of obeticholic acid tablets and directed companies to recall the chronic liver disease medication pending a fresh safety review. The DCGI sought cancellation of licenses for 5mg and 10mg tablets approved in March 2020 to treat primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), following recommendations from CDSCO's expert panel on gastroenterology and hepatology. Global regulators, including the USFDA and European Medicines Agency, recommended revocation due to risks of serious liver injury and lack of confirmed clinical efficacy.
items.title: India Halts Obeticholic Acid Production and Orders Recall Pending Safety Review

items.summary: On November 13th, 2026, the author released datasette-cluster-map version 0.19, one of their oldest and favorite Datasette plugins. It now works with Datasette 1.0a42 and depends on the new datasette-leaflet to request OpenStreetMap tiles with a referrer header. The release includes a map of power plants owned by California's PG&E, demonstrating Datasette's recently redesigned facets.
items.title: datasette-cluster-map 0.19

items.summary: Dayana Blanco Quiroga, an Aymara Indigenous woman from Bolivia's west, co-founded the Uru Uru Team in 2019 to clean the toxic, nearly drained 83-square-mile Uru Uru Lake by hand. The documentary How to Plant a Lake follows her eight-step effort: digging marsh totora plants and transplanting them into polluted water where they absorb heavy metals while being cordoned off from animals. Beyond mining waste dumped near Oruro since the 1990s, drought tied to El Niño and climate change nearly emptied the lake a decade ago. Blanco hopes future generations can say 'we fought for our lake.'
items.title: How a Bolivian Woman Is Reviving a Dying Lake with Plants

items.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders frames the Democratic Senate leadership contest between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen not as a personality fight but as a defining debate over the party's future direction. The race, he argues, determines whether Democrats preserve an establishment model reliant on billionaire donors, consultants and TV ads or transform into a grassroots movement for working families.
items.title: What the Schumer–Van Hollen Senate Leadership Race Is Really About

items.summary: Datasette table pages previously sent a Referrer-Policy: no-referrer header, which caused plugins loading tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. The datasette-leaflet plugin now sets the referrer policy on tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, passing only the host rather than the full page path. This change lets other Datasette plugins depend on the bundled Leaflet while respecting OSM's hosted tile server requirements.
items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3 fixes OpenStreetMap referrer policy on tile requests

items.summary: Rinnai launched the REHPW series of electric heat pump water heaters, adding Wi-Fi controls to an appliance that uses less electricity than conventional resistance models. Available in 50-, 65- and 80-gallon sizes with UEF ratings up to 4.0, the units deliver up to 91 gallons per hour and offer top-and-side plumbing connections for simpler installation.
items.title: Rinnai REHPW Heat Pump Water Heaters Add Wi-Fi and Easier Installation

items.summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are expected to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting on the sidelines of next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen. Discussions could cover nuclear stockpiles and the war with Iran, though not Ukraine. The three leaders lead the world's largest nuclear powers amid heightened tensions.
items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Set for Unprecedented Trilateral Meeting in China

items.summary: A freighter named Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked cruise ship The American Heritage near New Orleans' port Friday, causing it to capsize. Over 30 people were hospitalized—none critically—but no deaths occurred; at least 180 passengers and crew were rescued. Mayor Helena Moreno called it "a miracle on the Mississippi." The vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, was mid-eight-day cruise.
items.title: Tanker Collides with Cruise Ship on Mississippi in New Orleans

items.summary: The FAA is expanding its $875 million SMART system, an AI tool advising controllers on scheduling and routing, from the National Capital Region to all 22 national airspace centers. Since launching over Washington, DC airspace in September, it rerouted 180 flights, saving about 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight. Airlines support the rollout; the controller union says it was not involved. Human specialists still validate recommendations before use.
items.title: FAA Expands AI Air-Traffic Tool Nationwide After DC Success

items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa announced that the EU would send a diplomatic team, not a single envoy, to upcoming Ukraine talks alongside five Coalition of the Willing nations: the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland. The move addresses fears that US-led negotiations could sideline Europe while Moscow and Washington shape the conflict's outcome. Leaders remain divided over representation—Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov demanded one European voice, but a team was chosen instead to include coalition members like the UK. Optimism is tempered by pessimism: Donald Tusk dismissed talks as exaggerated, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned of an 'Anchorage moment,' and Andris Kulbergs stressed Europe's collective strength.
items.title: EU Sends Five-Power Diplomatic Team for Ukraine Talks Amid Disputes Over Representation and Timing

items.summary: India's merchandise exports reached a record $49.47 billion in October 2026, up 45% year-on-year and the fastest monthly growth in five years, per commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal. Petroleum products drove export gains (+140%), while imports rose 16.51% to $89.35 billion as West Asian conflict pushed crude near $120 a barrel; India sources over 85% of its crude abroad. The trade deficit narrowed to $39.88 billion, and combined goods-and-services exports also hit an all-time high.
items.title: India's October Merchandise Exports Hit Record High Amid Rising Oil Imports

items.summary: Police and the Special Operations Group busted a fake-currency operation in Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh, arresting Reena, Akil, Suhail, Imran and Ashutosh while recovering counterfeit notes worth Rs 1.15 lakh plus Rs 37,000 in genuine currency. The gang printed fake Rs 500 notes on GSM paper using portable equipment taught online.
items.title: Counterfeit currency racket busted in Shahjahanpur; Rs 1.15 lakh seized, five arrested

items.summary: A UN official warned that rising attacks on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab threaten global peace, stability and economic security. Khaled Khiari told the Security Council that maritime incidents have increased, with October recording the highest monthly toll since February per the International Maritime Organization (IMO), which logged 134 confirmed incidents as of November 11. Twenty-five seafarers were killed. Restrictions raised energy, transport and insurance costs while threatening food security amid constrained fertilizer shipments. Though much energy export capacity has recovered through alternative routes, Khiari cautioned that this does not signal a return to normal conditions. He urged Iran and the United States to pursue good-faith diplomacy in Doha, warning against using chokepoints as instruments of coercion.
items.title: UN Urges Restoration of Safe Navigation in Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea

items.summary: Two readers respond to an article about UK public bodies overwhelmed by chatbot-produced complaints. A nine-year housing-association complaint investigator describes how the role has changed dramatically, noting that hundreds of pages of wordy submissions now arrive and that customers often cannot follow the technical language used in their own letters; she argues human-written complaints are more useful because they reveal genuine need. She adds that AI lets regular complainants flood her organisation with multiple large monthly submissions, which makes staff feel disrespected and prompts plans to treat this as harassment.
items.title: How it feels to battle with a flood of AI-generated complaints

items.summary: On Nov. 14, 2026 Türkiye published a law ratifying the Aug. 7, 2026 Mecca Agreement for Joint Defense between Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The parliament approved it with 279 votes to 119 among 398 lawmakers present in the 592-member body. Under the pact, the three nations pledged collective security, deeper defense cooperation and regional stability.
items.title: Türkiye Ratifies Mecca Joint Defense Pact With Pakistan and Saudi Arabia

items.summary: Volkswagen reportedly filed trademarks for 'ID. UP' on October 22, 2026, potentially naming its upcoming €20,000 ($22,000) entry-level electric car launching in 2027. The model will use a 37 kWh LFP battery and seat four passengers with 305 liters of luggage space.
items.title: Volkswagen's Next Affordable EV May Be Named ID. UP
